name: es30-integer-float-textures
title: Integer, float and packed-float textures
summary: usampler2D/isampler2D lookups return the stored integers bit for bit (R8UI, R16I, RGBA8I, RGBA16UI, R32I above 2^24, RGBA32UI, RGB10_A2UI); float and half-float textures (R32F, RGBA32F, RGBA16F, R16F) return exact floats; R11F_G11F_B10F and RGB9_E5 decode as specified (and RGB9_E5 encodes as specified). Values are read back through RGBA32UI/RGBA32I render targets (floatBitsToUint). Integer textures are complete only with NEAREST filters (initial filters make them incomplete, a sampler object repairs that, NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST chains work); 16-bit and packed formats filter, R32F follows GL_OES_texture_float_linear; GenerateMipmap and format-combination errors.
spec: ES 3.0 §3.8.3 Texture Image Specification (Tables 3.2, 3.3, 3.13: valid format/type/internalformat combinations, color-renderable and texture-filterable columns), §3.8.3.2 Encoding of Special Internal Formats (RGB9_E5 encoding)
ES 3.0 §2.1.3, §2.1.4 Unsigned 11-bit and 10-bit Floating-Point Numbers; §3.7.2 Transfer of Pixel Rectangles (UNSIGNED_INT_10F_11F_11F_REV, UNSIGNED_INT_5_9_9_9_REV)

ES 3.0 §3.8.13 Texture Completeness (not texture-filterable formats need NEAREST / NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST), §3.8.13.1 Effects of Sampler Objects on Texture Completeness, §3.8.14 Texture State (initial filters)

ES 3.0 §3.8.10 Texture Minification (3.8.10.2 bilinear weights, 3.8.10.5 Manual Mipmap Generation: INVALID_OPERATION unless color-renderable and texture-filterable), §3.8.17 Shared Exponent Texture Color Conversion

ES 3.0 §2.12.9.2 Texel Fetches, §2.12.9.4 / §3.9.2.1 Texture Access (incomplete texture returns (0, 0, 0, 1)), §2.12.9.7 Validation (two sampler types on one unit); ES 3.2 §11.1.3.5 (integer sampler on an incomplete texture: undefined)
ES 3.0 §4.3.2 Reading Pixels (RGBA_INTEGER with INT / UNSIGNED_INT), Table 3.13 (RGBA32UI / RGBA32I are color-renderable)

GLSL ES 3.00 §4.1.7 Samplers, §4.5.3 Default Precision Qualifiers (samplers are lowp by default), §8.8 Texture Lookup Functions (sampler / format combinations, texelFetch, textureLod), §8.3 floatBitsToUint

api.glGenTextures: one texture per format (15), the mip-chain texture, the initial-state texture and scratch textures
api.glBindTexture: textures on unit 0 for the exact path and the display pass; the second unit for the sampler-type check
api.glActiveTexture: unit 0 / unit 1 selection; the usampler2D and the sampler2D of the mixed-type program sit on different units in the positive control
api.glTexImage2D: R8UI, R16I, RGBA8I, RGBA16UI, R32I, RGBA32UI, RGB10_A2UI, R32F, RGBA32F, RGBA16F (HALF_FLOAT), R16F (FLOAT), R11F_G11F_B10F, RGB9_E5 (packed words and FLOAT data; the FLOAT encoding strict, ANGLE XFAIL) uploads: every texel read back exactly through the sampler; a 4-level R32I mip chain; INVALID_OPERATION for five invalid format/type/internalformat combinations, RGBA8UI accepted
api.glTexParameteri: NEAREST min/mag filters (typed glTexParameter overloads) make the textures complete; NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST on the integer mip chain
api.glGetTexParameteriv: initial MIN_FILTER = NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR and MAG_FILTER = LINEAR of a new integer texture
api.glGenerateMipmap: INVALID_OPERATION on R8UI, R32I, RGBA16UI, RGBA32UI (not filterable) and RGB9_E5 (not renderable); no error on RGBA8
api.glSamplerParameteri: MIN/MAG filters and CLAMP_TO_EDGE wrap of the two samplers: they decide completeness and filtering of the unit (exact words / filtered means)
api.glBindSampler: a NEAREST sampler makes an R32I texture with its incomplete initial state return exact values; a LINEAR sampler filters RGBA16F, R11F_G11F_B10F, RGB9_E5 and decides R32F completeness
api.glGenRenderbuffers: RGBA32UI and RGBA32I render targets of the exact path
api.glRenderbufferStorage: RGBA32UI and RGBA32I storage (color-renderable integer formats): rendered 32-bit words read back
api.glGenFramebuffers: framebuffer objects of the exact path
api.glBindFramebuffer: FRAMEBUFFER target: exact path versus the window
api.glFramebufferRenderbuffer: RGBA32UI / RGBA32I attached to COLOR_ATTACHMENT0; framebuffer complete
api.glCheckFramebufferStatus: FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE with RGBA32UI and RGBA32I attachments
api.glReadPixels: RGBA_INTEGER with UNSIGNED_INT (uint, float bit patterns) and INT: the exact 32-bit words of every texel compared with the CPU model; RGBA/UNSIGNED_BYTE of the window cells (display mapping)
api.glGetUniformLocation: u_tex, u_mode, u_lod, u_uv_shift, u_origin, u_scale, u_bias, u_gray, u_use_texture, u_zero, u_float_tex, u_uint_tex located
api.glUniform1i: sampler units, u_mode (texture / texelFetch / textureLod), u_lod, u_gray, u_use_texture; the two-sampler-types error depends on the unit values
api.glUniform1f: u_zero = 0 keeps the int(float(x)) comparison alive (the right half of cell 4 shows green/red stripes only with it)
api.glUniform2f: u_uv_shift: half a texel; the filtered lookups land exactly between two texels
api.glUniform2i: u_origin of each cell; probes at texel centers match the CPU mapping
api.glUniform3f: u_scale and u_bias: the displayed colors match the CPU mapping
api.glDrawArrays: TRIANGLE_STRIP quads from gl_VertexID for the exact path and every cell; the mixed-type draw raises (or, on Mesa, fails to raise) INVALID_OPERATION
api.glViewport: 8 x 8 exact-path viewport and the 64 x 64 cell viewports

visual_review.notes: 256x256 radeonsi es-max capture viewed at 3x (llvmpipe and zink captures differ by at most 1/255 per channel). 4x4 contact sheet of 8x8-texel cells, one texel per 8x8-pixel block. Row 0: a gray R8UI ramp, a gray R16I ramp, an RGBA8I cell with a blue checker (sign bit) over red/green ramps, an RGBA16UI color gradient. Row 1: the 2^24 cell with a clean gray ramp in the left half of every block and green/red vertical stripes in the right half (even texels green, odd red: float cannot hold odd integers above 2^24), a gray R32I ramp over the full int range, RGBA32UI and RGB10_A2UI color gradients. Row 2: R32F gray ramp with one black (-FLT_MAX) and one white (FLT_MAX) texel at the top, RGBA32F and RGBA16F color gradients, R16F gray ramp with a black and a white texel at the top right. Row 3: R11F_G11F_B10F, RGB9_E5 from packed words (a black texel for the tiny 2^-24 value and a white one for the maximum, top right) and RGB9_E5 from FLOAT data as smooth gradients, and the R32F gradient again through a LINEAR sampler (identical to the R32F cell, as expected when GL_OES_texture_float_linear is present).
